sentences: This time next year, I'll be working for a tech company in the Smart Village.
في مثل هذا الوقت من العام القادم، سأكون أعمل في شركة تكنولوجيا في القرية الذكية.
By 2040, scientists will have found cures for many diseases.
بحلول عام ٢٠٤٠، سيكون العلماء قد وجدوا علاجات لكثير من الأمراض.
In ten years' time, most people will be driving electric cars.
بعد عشر سنوات من الآن، سيكون معظم الناس يقودون سيارات كهربائية.
Don't call me at eight — I'll be watching the launch online.
لا تتصل بي في الثامنة؛ سأكون أشاهد الإطلاق على الإنترنت.
By the time you get home, the update will have finished.
بحلول الوقت الذي تصل فيه إلى البيت، سيكون التحديث قد انتهى.
Will you be using your laptop this evening?
هل ستستخدم حاسوبك المحمول هذا المساء؟
The researchers have made an important breakthrough.
حقق الباحثون إنجازًا علميًا مهمًا.
There isn't enough evidence to prove it yet.
لا توجد أدلة كافية لإثبات ذلك حتى الآن.
Egypt is investing in solar energy in Aswan.
تستثمر مصر في الطاقة الشمسية في أسوان.
By the end of this level, I'll have learnt 360 new words.
بنهاية هذا المستوى، سأكون قد تعلمت ٣٦٠ كلمة جديدة.

grammar.intro_en:
Future continuous: will be + -ing = an action in progress at a time in the future. At nine tomorrow, I'll be flying to Aswan.
Future perfect: will have + past participle = an action finished before a time in the future. By Friday, I'll have finished the project.
grammar.intro_ar: العربية تستخدم «سـ / سوف» لكل المستقبل تقريبًا، أما الإنجليزية فتفرّق: «سأكون أعمل» (حدث مستمر في لحظة معينة في المستقبل) = will be working، و«سأكون قد أنهيت» (حدث سينتهي قبل لحظة معينة في المستقبل) = will have finished. الخطأ الشائع: By next year I will finish my degree، والأصح مع by أن نقول will have finished. وبعد by the time و when نستخدم المضارع البسيط وليس will: By the time you arrive (وليس will arrive).

rows: in progress at a future moment
This time tomorrow, I'll be sitting my exam.
Will you be coming to the meeting?
By 2030, they will have built the new city.
I won't have finished by six.

notes: Time words: future continuous → at this time tomorrow, this time next week, at 8 p.m. · future perfect → by, by the time, by the end of, before.
Wrong: By the time you will arrive … ✔ By the time you arrive …
Stative verbs (know, believe, own) don't usually take -ing: By June, I'll have known her for ten years.

exercises.title: Exercise 1 · Future continuous or future perfect? Choose.
exercises.instructions: Future continuous or future perfect? Choose.
items: 1) Don't phone at seven. We (will be having / will have had) dinner.
2) This time next week, Omar (will be lying / will have lain) on the beach in Hurghada.
3) By the end of the year, I (will be saving / will have saved) 20,000 pounds.
4) By 2035, scientists (will be sending / will have sent) people to Mars.
5) By the time the film starts, we (will be finishing / will have finished) our popcorn.
6) (Will you be using / Will you have used) the car tomorrow morning?

exercises.title: Exercise 2 · Complete with the future continuous or the future perfect.
exercises.instructions: Complete with the future continuous or the future perfect.
items: 1) By Monday, the technician ___ (install) the new software.
2) By the time you read this message, I ___ (leave) Cairo.
3) At ten tomorrow, I ___ (take) my driving test.
4) She ___ (not finish) the report by Thursday — it's too long.
5) In twenty years' time, robots ___ (do) most of the housework.
6) ___ you ___ (work) late tonight?

exercises.title: Exercise 3 · Correct the mistake.
items: 1) By next June, I will finish my degree.
2) By the time she will arrive, we'll have eaten.
3) This time tomorrow I'll be fly to London.
4) By 2030, they will have build a new airport.
5) Call me later — at nine I will have watched the match.
6) In five years, I'll have living in Alexandria.
answers: 1) By next June, I will have finished my degree.
2) By the time she arrives, we'll have eaten.
3) This time tomorrow I'll be flying to London.
4) By 2030, they will have built a new airport.
5) …at nine I will be watching the match.
6) In five years, I'll be living in Alexandria.

exercises.title: Exercise 4 · Translate into English.
items: 1) في مثل هذا الوقت غدًا، سأكون مسافرًا إلى الأقصر.
2) بحلول عام ٢٠٣٠، سيكونون قد بنوا محطة طاقة شمسية جديدة.
3) هل ستستخدم الحاسوب الليلة؟
4) لن أكون قد أنهيت المشروع بحلول يوم الخميس.
5) حقق العلماء اكتشافًا مهمًا.
answers: 1) This time tomorrow, I'll be travelling to Luxor. / This time tomorrow, I'll be flying (going) to Luxor.
2) By 2030, they will have built a new solar power station. / By 2030, they will have built a new solar power plant.
3) Will you be using the computer tonight?
4) I won't have finished the project by Thursday.
5) Scientists have made an important discovery. / Scientists made an important discovery.

write_speak: Write & Speak — “Life in 2040”: write 150–200 words about how science and technology will change your life and the world. Use the future continuous and the future perfect at least three times each. Then give a two-minute talk about your predictions.
other: Example: I think that by 2040 technology will have changed our lives completely. First of all, I believe that most people won't be driving their own cars. Driverless taxis will be taking us to work, and we will be using that time to read, rest or study. In Cairo, the traffic problem might finally be solved! Secondly, I am sure that scientists will have made huge breakthroughs in medicine. They will have found cures for some kinds of cancer, and doctors will be checking our health through small devices that we wear on our wrists. Energy will also be different. By 2040, Egypt will have built many more solar parks like the one in Benban near Aswan, and our homes will be using clean, renewable energy. As for me, I will be fifty years old. I hope I will be working from home three days a week and spending more time with my family. By then, I will have visited at least ten countries, and I will have learnt a third language — maybe Chinese!
